plain.headline: A Light for All Nations
plain.intro: Epiphany means showing or appearing, and today God shows his Son to the whole world. Isaiah sees nations streaming toward the light of Jerusalem with gold and frankincense, and Paul says the Gentiles now share fully in God's promise. In the Gospel, wise men from the east follow a star to worship the newborn King.
plain.listen: the star, and the three gifts the wise men open

Reading 1.box: Isaiah tells Jerusalem that although darkness covers the earth, God's glory will shine on her. People from far away will come to her light, bringing her children home and carrying rich gifts. The Church hears in these words the coming of the wise men to Jesus.

chunks.text: Rise up and shine, for your light has come. The glory of the Lord is shining on you. Darkness covers the earth, and deep darkness covers the peoples. But the Lord will rise on you, and his glory will be seen on you.

Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn. Look up and look around: they are all gathering and coming to you. Your sons are coming from far away, and your daughters are being carried in their arms.

Then you will see and shine with joy, and your heart will swell and overflow. The riches of the sea will be brought to you, and the wealth of the nations will come to you. Crowds of camels will fill your land, young camels from Midian and Ephah. Everyone from Sheba will come, bringing gold and frankincense and singing the praises of the Lord.

Responsorial Psalm.box: The psalm prays for a king who rules with justice and protects the poor. It pictures kings from distant lands bringing him gifts and bowing before him, and the Church hears in it Christ the King.

Reading 2.box: Paul says God has shown him a mystery that was hidden from earlier generations. The Gentiles, people who are not Jewish, now share in God's promise and belong to the same body in Christ.

chunks.text: You have surely heard that God gave me the gift of his grace to share with you. He made his hidden plan known to me, as I have already written to you briefly.

In earlier times this plan was not made known to people. Now the Spirit has revealed it to his holy apostles and prophets. Here is the plan: through the Good News, the Gentiles share the inheritance. They belong to the same body and share in the same promise in Christ Jesus.

Gospel.box: Wise men from the east see a star and come looking for a newborn king. King Herod, who ruled Judea under Rome, is troubled and plots in secret, but the wise men find the child and worship him. Christians have long seen the gold as a gift for a king, the frankincense as a gift for God, and the myrrh as a sign of his death and burial.

chunks.text: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea while Herod was king. Wise men from the east came to Jerusalem and asked, "Where is the newborn King of the Jews? We saw his star in the east, and we have come to worship him."
When King Herod heard this, he was troubled, and so was all Jerusalem. He called together all the chief priests and teachers of the law and asked them where the Messiah was to be born.

They told him, "In Bethlehem of Judea. This is what the prophet wrote: 'And you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means the least among the rulers of Judah. From you will come a leader who will shepherd my people Israel.'"

Then Herod called the wise men in secret and found out from them exactly when the star had appeared. He sent them to Bethlehem and said, "Go and search carefully for the child. When you find him, come back and tell me, so that I can go and worship him too."

After hearing the king, they set out. The star they had seen in the east went ahead of them, until it stopped over the place where the child was. When they saw the star, they were filled with great joy.

They went into the house and saw the child with Mary his mother, and they knelt down and worshiped him. Then they opened their treasures and offered him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh. Warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, they returned to their own country by another road.

plain.carry: This week I will look for one way to share the light of Christ with someone who feels far from God.

kids.headline: Following the Star
kids.intro: Today is the feast of the Epiphany. Wise men from a faraway land follow a bright star to find baby Jesus. Jesus came for everyone in the whole world, near and far.
kids.listen: the three gifts the wise men bring to Jesus

Reading 1.box: Long before Jesus was born, the prophet Isaiah said a great light would shine on God's people. He said people would come from far away, riding camels and bringing gold and sweet-smelling incense.

chunks.text: Wake up and shine, because your light has come. God's glory is shining on you. The whole world is dark, but God's light shines on you, and kings from all over will come to that light.

Look around. People are coming from far away, and your children are coming home. You will glow with happiness. Riches will come to you from across the sea. Lots and lots of camels will come, carrying gold and incense, and everyone will sing praise to God.

Responsorial Psalm.box: This song prays for a king who is fair and good and who helps poor people. It says kings from faraway places will bring him gifts and bow down to him.

Reading 2.box: Saint Paul says God had a secret plan that he has now made known. Jesus came not only for one people, but for all the people of the world.

chunks.text: God gave me a special job: to share his gift of love with you. God showed me his secret plan. Long ago, people did not know this plan. Now God's Spirit has shown it to the apostles and prophets. Here it is: people from every nation are part of God's family, and God's promises in Jesus are for them too.

Gospel.box: Wise men from the east saw a star in the sky and knew a great king had been born. They traveled a long way to find him. King Herod also wanted to find Jesus, but not for a good reason.

chunks.text: After Jesus was born in Bethlehem, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem. They asked, "Where is the baby who was born to be King of the Jews? We saw his star, and we came to worship him." King Herod heard this and was upset. He asked the priests and teachers where the promised King would be born.

They said, "In Bethlehem. A prophet wrote that a leader would come from Bethlehem to take care of God's people like a shepherd." Herod secretly asked the wise men when they first saw the star. Then he sent them to Bethlehem and said, "Find the child and come tell me, so I can worship him too."

The wise men set out, and the star went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where Jesus was. They were so happy. They went into the house and saw Jesus with Mary, his mother. They knelt down, worshiped him, and gave him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh. A dream warned them not to go back to Herod, so they went home a different way.

word.meaning: Epiphany means showing. On this day we remember how God showed Jesus to people from all over the world.

kids.draw: Draw the wise men following a bright star, and draw a gift you would like to bring to Jesus.
kids.ask: The wise men gave Jesus their best treasures, so what is something you could give Jesus this week?

family.opener: Today we remember the wise men who followed a star a long way to find Jesus and bring him their best gifts.
questions: What helps our family find our way to Jesus, the way the star led the wise men?
The wise men went home by another way after meeting Jesus, so how has knowing Jesus changed the way we live?
Who do we know who feels far away or left out, and how can we help them feel welcome?
family.try: Each evening this week, light a candle at dinner, name one person who needs the light of Jesus, and pray for them together.
family.pray: Lord Jesus, light of the world, lead our family to you as the star led the wise men, and help us share your light with everyone we meet.
